corrections.correction: Jose Antonio Carrillo, First Alcalde / President of the Ayuntamiento of Los Angeles (pueblo grant, April 8, 1828), NOT Gov. Echeandia. Per Board opinion transcript p17 and Carrillo's deposition transcript p9-10.
corrections.evidence: This is a PUEBLO grant, not a gubernatorial grant. The concession was made by Jose Antonio Carrillo, First Alcalde / President of the Ayuntamiento of Los Angeles, decree dated April 8, 1828 (grant translation, transcript p12, PDF p13: '...Carrillo'). Carrillo's own deposition (transcript p9-10, PDF p15-16): 'A paper is now shown me purporting to be a permission to occupy land given to Antonio Jose Roca and Nemesio Dominguez dated April 8 1828. My own genuine signature is on said paper... I was at the time First Alcalde and Judge of the First Instance... I was President of the Ayuntamiento.' Board opinion (transcript p17, PDF p23): 'a grant issued by Jose Antonio Carrillo Alcalde of the Los Angeles District bearing date the 8th day of April 1828.' Echeandia (the register's value) had no part in it; Hoffman's 'Jose Antonio Carrillo' agrees with the case file.

corrections.correction: Manuel Jimeno (Casarin), 1st vocal of the departmental junta in exercise of the government, per grant decree transcript p.11: 'Manuel Jimeno Casarin 1er Vocal propietario de la Exma Junta Departamental en ejercicio del Gobierno del mismo'
corrections.evidence: Decree transcript p.11 (PDF p17): 'El Sor Dn Manuel Jimeno Casarin, 1er Vocal propietario de la Exma Junta Departamental en ejercicio del Gobierno del mismo asi lo mando decreto y firmo... Jimeno'. Titulo header transcript p.12 (PDF p18) repeats 'Manuel Jimeno Casarin... en ejercicio del Gobierno'. Register 'Alvarado' is wrong; Hoffman ('Manuel Jimeno') agrees with the case file.

corrections.correction: Manuel Jimeno (Casarin), 1st vocal in exercise of the government, per grant decree transcript p.10; Alvarado's role was limited to ratifying the departmental assembly's approval in 1840
corrections.evidence: Decree transcript p.10 (PDF p15): 'El Senor Dn Manuel Jimeno Casarin primer vocal propietario de la Excma Junta del Departto de las Californias, lo mando, Decreto y firmo de que Doy fee. Manuel Jimeno'; translation p.16: 'Don Manuel Jimeno Casarin 1st Member of the Most Excellent Assembly... ordered, decreed & signed it'. Alvarado only ratified the junta approval later (13 June 1840, transcript p.11). Register 'Alvarado' is wrong; Hoffman ('Manuel Jimeuo' = Jimeno, OCR-garbled) agrees with the case file.

corrections.correction: Jose Castro, Prefect of the First District (San Jose), who issued and signed the grant 10 Aug 1839 under authority delegated to prefects by Governor Alvarado's administration (Ley Reglamentaria of 1837). Per grant instrument transcript p.27 and Board opinion transcript p.28. The register's 'Alvarado' identifies the delegating governor, not the actual grantor; Hoffman's 'Jose Castro' is the granting officer of record.
corrections.evidence: This is a PREFECT grant, not a gubernatorial concession. Grant instrument transcript p.27: 'The Same Dn Jose Castro Prefect of the 1st District that orders decrees and signs which I attest. Jose Castro / Jose Ma Covarrubias Secy.' Board opinion transcript p.28: 'a grant issued by Jose Castro... the said Castro was the prefect of the district in which the land was situated at the time of the issue of the grant, and that his signature attached to said grant is genuine... the land was comprised of a part of the common lands of the Pueblo of San Jose'. Alvarado's own deposition transcript p.21 (PDF p25): 'The Prefectures were established during my administration as Governor, I issued an order conferring authority upon the Prefect of the first District to grant lands... Jose Castro was Prefect of the first District at the time that this document bears date, and was clothed with such authority'. Register 'Alvarado' names the delegating governor, not the granting officer; Hoffman ('Jose Castro') matches the grantor of record.

corrections.correction: Manuel Jimeno (acting governor / gobernador interino), per grant stamped p14-15: 'Manuel Jimeno Casarin... en ejercicio del gobierno del mismo... Dado en Monterrey a siete de Septiembre de mil ochocientos treinta y nueve. Manl. Jimeno.' Not Alvarado.
corrections.evidence: Grant (stamped p14): 'Manuel Jimeno Casarin primer Vocal propietario de la Exma Junta del Departamento de las Californias en ejercicio del gobierno del mismo', signed 'Manl. Jimeno' (stamped p15); translation (stamped p26): 'Acting as Governor of the same'; DC opinion (stamped p171): 'a grant from Jimeno the Governor ad interim of California'. Alvarado's name appears only on the testimonio of the Junta's 26 May 1840 approval, issued 23 July 1840 (stamped pp16-17), which likely caused the register's error. Hoffman agrees with the case file.

corrections.correction: Jose de la Guerra y Noriega, acting as military commandant of the southern portion under Don Luis Arguello (who exercised the civil functions of Governor) - PDF p47. NOT Micheltorena.
corrections.evidence: Board opinion PDF p47 (stamped PAGE 39): 'The grant was made by Don Jose de la Guerra y Noriega then acting as military commandant of the southern portion of the Territory, under Don Luis Arguello, who was in command at Monterey and exercised the civil functions of Governor'. Micheltorena appears only as the official who in 1843 referred the Abila-Sanchez boundary dispute to three commissioners (PDF p46, stamped PAGE 38)

corrections.correction: Manuel Jimeno per the grant's sworn translation, PDF p31: 'Given in Monterey the sixteenth day of October Eighteen hundred and thirty nine / Manuel Jimeno / Francisco Arce, First Official'
corrections.evidence: The grant itself is signed by Manuel Jimeno, not Alvarado. Sworn translation, PDF p31 (stamped PAGE 24): 'Given in Monterey the sixteenth day of October Eighteen hundred and thirty nine / Manuel Jimeno / Francisco Arce, First Official'. The petition, PDF p9 (stamped PAGE 4), likewise says 'a decree issued on the same day under the signature of Manuel Jimeno, first Vocal of the Departmental Assembly declaring your petitioner the lawful Owner of said land'. Alvarado's name appears nowhere in the pages read

corrections.correction: Manuel Jimeno (acting Governor of California), per petition PDF p11 / transcript p5: 'on the 4th day of September A.D. 1839, Manuel Jimeno Governor of California... granted to Edward Manuel McIntosh'; corroborated by James Black deposition PDF p13. Not Alvarado.
corrections.evidence: The grant was signed by Manuel Jimeno, NOT Alvarado. Petition (PDF p11, transcript p5): 'on the 4th day of September A.D. 1839, Manuel Jimeno Governor of California by virtue of authority in him vested, granted to Edward Manuel McIntosh'; James Black deposition (PDF p13): 'Governor Jimeno gave McIntosh a title to this Rancho in 1839.' Alvarado was the constitutional governor and the Departmental Junta approval of 22 May 1840 fell in his term, which likely produced the register's error; but the concession itself was made by Jimeno as acting governor. Hoffman ('Manuel Jimeno') agrees with the case file against the register.

corrections.correction: Luis Antonio Arguello, governor of Alta California under Mexico, per petition PDF p9 / transcript p5 and the depositions of Cantua, Vallejo, Soberanes and Spence. Register's 'a Spanish governor' is wrong on both count and era: the petition claims 'under a Mexican Grant' (PDF p8).
corrections.evidence: PDF p9 (transcript p5): 'The Original Title was derived of Governor Don Luis Antonio Arguello in 1823'; PDF p16 (transcript p12) David Spence's own deposition: 'the Rancho Llano de Buenavista had been granted to the said Jose Mariano Estrada by Don Luis Arguello Governor of Upper California in the year 1823'; PDF p10 (transcript p6) Guadalupe Cantua: 'It was granted to said Estrada by Luis Arguello Governor in 1823'; PDF p14 (transcript p10) Mariano Soberanes: 'granted in 1823 by Governor Arguello to Mariano Estrada'. The petition itself, PDF p8, styles it 'a Mexican Grant' - Arguello was the first governor under Mexican rule, not a Spanish governor.

corrections.correction: Nicolas Gutierrez granted El Molino (1836); Figueroa granted only the exchanged-away Ojotska tract (Dec 1833). Per petition transcript p4 and Vallejo deposition transcript p7; Hoffman corroborates 'Feb. 24th 1836, by Nicolas Gutierrez'.
corrections.evidence: The El Molino (Molinos) tract was granted by NICOLAS GUTIERREZ, not Figueroa. Petition (transcript p4): 'Nicolas Gutierez Governor of California by virtue of authority in him vested Issued to the petitioner a title for the aforesaid tract of Levanta hyeme.' Vallejo (transcript p7, who as Cooper's agent handled the exchange and got the El Molino title): 'granted... in 1836 by Governor Gutierez... The arrangement was made with Governor Figueroa before his death, but was completed by Governor Gutierez.' Figueroa granted only the exchanged-away Ojotska tract (decree transcript p25, título p27, Dec 1833).

corrections.correction: Jose Figueroa (Jefe Superior Politico of Alta California), PDF p27 and PDF p29-30.
corrections.evidence: PDF p27 (PAGE 21): 'El Senor Don Jose Figueroa, general de Brigada, Comandante general, Inspector y Jefe Superior Politico del Territorio de la Alta California asi lo mando, decreto y firmo' (signed Jose Figueroa / Agustin V. Zamorano Srio.); PDF p29-30 (PAGES 23-24) titulo issued in Figueroa's name. Not a Spanish governor: the grant is Mexican-era.

corrections.correction: Luis Antonio Arguello ('Gefe Superior Politico y Militar', PDF 27-28; DC decree tp69 'Antonio Arguello then Governor of California') for the original 1823 grant; Figueroa for the 1834 addition, approved by Alvarado 1840. Register 'Castro' is wrong
corrections.evidence: Register 'Castro' is wrong. Original grantor = Luis Antonio Arguello: Doc B petition addressed to 'Sr Gefe Supor Politico y Militar de la Na California, Captn Dn Luis Anto. Arguello', decree signed 'Luis Antonio Arguello, Gefe Superior Politico y Militar de esta Provincia de la Alta California' (PDF 27-28). DC decree tp69: 'granted to Francisco Maria Ruiz by Antonio Arguello then Governor of California on the 15th day of June A.D. 1823'. The 1834 addition was by Figueroa, approved 1840 by Alvarado. Jose Castro appears nowhere in this file. Hoffman ('Luis Antonio Arguello') agrees with the file against the register

corrections.correction: Micheltorena, per the decrees signed by him at Monterey in Oct 1843 (p45, p46). Register 'Figueroa' is not supported by any document in the case file.
corrections.evidence: p45 marginal decree 'Monterey Oct [2]4 1843. Let the Secretary of State of this Supreme Departmental Government report. (signed) Micheltorena'; p46 'In conformity with the report, let the title be issued with the conditions of the law. (signed) Micheltorena'. No Figueroa document appears anywhere in the expediente; the only granting governor of record is Micheltorena.

corrections.correction: Jose Ramon Estrada (Prefect) for the Buelna tract; Manuel Jimeno (1st Vocal of the Departmental Junta, acting Governor) for the Arana tract (opinion p70, p74)
corrections.evidence: Opinion p70/decree p75: 'Jose Ramon Estrada' as Prefect (register gives wrong initial 'Jose E.'); opinion p74: 'Manuel Jimeno, 1st Vocal of the Departmental Junta acting as Governor' approving/granting the Arana tract (register gives 'Jose Jimeno')

corrections.correction: Not a Spanish governor. The granting authority of record is the Mexican political chief / acting governor of Alta California in 1835, named in the claimants' petition (PDF p19 / stamped p17) as Jose Castro, with the Territorial Deputation's approval of 18 Dec 1835.
corrections.evidence: The operative documents are of November 1835, i.e. the MEXICAN period, not Spanish. Claimants' petition PDF p19 (stamped p17) names the granting officer: the October 1835 decree in their favour 'was made on the 3rd day of October 1835 by Don Jose Castro who was on that day the Political Chief or Governor of Alta California', and it was 'the said Governor or Political Chief' who on 26 November 1835 issued the decree of concession. No Spanish-period title paper appears among the exhibits, and the Board's opinion (PDF p429-431 / stamped p383-385) rests entirely on the 1835 documents.

corrections.correction: Manuel Jimeno (acting/interim Governor, 'Gobernador Interino'), per the concession decree of 21 Dec 1842 (transcript p.16): 'El Exmo Senor Gobernador asi lo mando decreto y firmo. Jimeno', confirmed by the judicial possession (transcript p.22): 'conferido por el Exmo Sr Gobernador Interino del Departamento Dn Manuel Jimeno' and by the Board's own opinion. Register 'Alvarado' is wrong; Alvarado only referred the petition to the Prefect on 11 Aug 1842
corrections.evidence: The GRANT was made by Manuel Jimeno as acting governor, NOT Alvarado. Concession decree (image 22, transcript p.16): 'Monterrey. 21 de Dbre de 1842... El Exmo Senor Gobernador asi lo mando decreto y firmo. Jimeno'; judicial possession (image 30, transcript p.22): 'el respetivo titulo que se le ha conferido por el Exmo Sr Gobernador Interino del Departamento Dn Manuel Jimeno con fecha veinte y uno de Diciembre de mil ochocientos quarenta y dos'; Board opinion (image 57, transcript p.31): 'It was granted on the 21st of December 1842 by Manuel Jimeno Vocal of the Departmental Assembly and acting Governor of California to Jose Antonio Estudillo'. Alvarado appears in the espediente only as the governor who on 11 Aug 1842 referred the petition to the Prefect (marginal order, image 26), a preliminary step, not the grant

corrections.correction: Manuel Micheltorena, not Alvarado. Grant decree PDF p18 (transcript p14): 'Manuel Michelttorena Gobernador Comandante General e Ynspector de ambas Californias'; signed 'Man.l Michellt.a', PDF p19.
corrections.evidence: The grant decree is Micheltorena's, not Alvarado's. PDF p18 (transcript p14): 'Manuel Michelttorena Gobernador Comandante General e Ynspector de ambas Californias. Por cuanto el Ciudadano Maximo Alaniz, ha pretendido para su beneficio personal i el de su familia el parage conocido con el nombre de San Jose Buenos Ayres'; signed PDF p19 'Man.l Michellt.a'. Sworn translation PDF p26 (transcript p22): '(Grant.) Manuel Michelttorena, Governor, Commandant General and Inspector of both Californias.' Abel Stearns authenticated 'The signatures of Manuel Michletorena, Francisco Arce ... I believe to be genuine' (PDF p10, transcript p7). Petition PDF p7: 'by deed of grant made by Manuel Michaltorena as Governor of the Californias dated February 24th A.D. 1843'. Hoffman agrees against the register.

corrections.correction: Manuel Micheltorena. Title heading PDF p15 (transcript p9): 'Manuel Micheltorena, General de Brigada del Ejercito Mejicano ... y Gobernador del Departam.to de las Californias'. Alvarado's role was confined to the 1840-41 preliminaries on the 600-vara petition (his marginal decree PDF p24, transcript p18: 'Monterey Ag.to 10 de 1840. Informe el Mayordomo de S. Jose ... Alvarado').
corrections.evidence: Micheltorena granted the rancho. Title heading PDF p15 (transcript p9): 'Manuel Micheltorena, General de Brigada del Ejercito Mejicano, Ayudante Gral de la Plana Mayor y Comandante Gral y Gobernador del Departam.to de las Californias. Por cuanto D.n Guillermo Castro ha pretendido para su beneficio personal y el de su familia el terreno conocido con el nombre de San Lorenzo ... he venido en concederle el terreno mencionado, declarandole la propiedad de el por las presentes letras'; Micheltorena also signed the referral of 13 Oct 1843 (PDF p14, transcript p8, 'Monterey Oct.e 13 de 1843. Inf.e el S. S.rio del Despacho. Michellt.a') and the added condition of 24 Oct 1843 (PDF p16, transcript p10, 'Michellt.a'), on Manuel Jimeno's report of 23 Oct 1843 (PDF p15). Hoffman agrees against the register.

corrections.correction: Juan B. Alvarado per the expediente, authenticated by Alvarado himself (pdf p20), by J.J. Warner (pdf p27-28) and by Manuel Dominguez (pdf p98-99). Register's 'Figueroa' is wrong.
corrections.evidence: Granting governor is Juan B. Alvarado (with Juan Bandini as secretary), not Figueroa. Alvarado authenticated his own signature on the 1838 expediente (pdf p20, transcript p14-15); J.J. Warner (pdf p27-28, transcript p21-22): 'I am acquainted with the signatures of Juan B. Alvarado and Juan Bandini... their signatures in said original document... are genuine'; Manuel Dominguez (pdf p98-99, transcript) likewise authenticates the Alvarado order. Register 'Figueroa' is wrong; Hoffman 'Juan B. Alvarado' agrees. (A later augmentation was sought from Micheltorena/Pico, but the principal grant is Alvarado's.)

corrections.correction: Manuel Jimeno (Casarin), 1st vocal of the Departmental Junta in exercise of the government (acting governor), per titulo p16/p18: signed 'Man'l Jimeno', given Monterey 27 Sep 1841. Register's 'Alvarado' appears in the file only as the custom-house stamp-paper habilitation signature for 1839-40 (p17/p19), which may be the source of the confusion.
corrections.evidence: The grant was NOT made by Alvarado. Titulo stamped p15/p17: 'Manuel Jimeno Casarin 1st Regular Vocal of the Most Excellent Departmental Junta in exercise of the Government of the same... I have granted him the aforesaid land', signed 'Man'l Jimeno' (p16/p18). Board opinion p19: 'a grant made to the present claimant by Manuel Jimeno 1st Vocal... exercising the functions of Governor, dated September 27th 1841'; US brief p41 says the same. Hoffman ('Manuel Jimeno') agrees with the case file against the register.

corrections.correction: Manuel Jimeno (Jimeno Casarin), gobernador interino / acting governor, 30 July 1839 - per grant decree transcript p24 and U.S. court decree transcript p89-90; second grant 19 Nov 1845 by Pio Pico. NOT Alvarado.
corrections.evidence: Grant decree, transcript p24: 'El Senor Don Manuel Jimeno Casarin Gobernador Interino del Departamento de las Californias asi lo mando, decreto y firmo de que doy fe. Manuel Jimeno.' Court decree, transcript p89-90: 'granted to the said Francisco Cota ... the first by Manuel Jimeno, acting governor of said department, on the 30th day of July, 1839, and the second by governor Pio Pico on the 19th day of November, 1845.' Alvarado appears in this file ONLY on the later order of 10 June 1840 (transcript p25): 'El Sr. D. Juan B. Alvarado Gobernador Constitucional del Departamento de las Californias asi lo proveyo y firmo... Alvarado' - i.e. he ordered the testimonio of the Assembly's approval issued in confirmation of the terreno 'que otorgo en treinta de Julio de mil ochocientos treinta y nueve'. He did not make the concession.

corrections.correction: Manuel Micheltorena, alone (transcript p8/p15). Alvarado has no part in this grant.
corrections.evidence: The only granting officer in the file is Micheltorena. Transcript p8: 'Manuel Micheltorena General de Brigada del Ejercito Mejicano Gobernador y Comandante General del departamento de ambas Californias ... he venido en concederle exclusivte. la Isla mencionada declarandoles la propriedad de ella por las presentes letras'. Translation p15: 'Manuel Micheltorena General of Brigade of the Mexican Army Governor & commanding General of the Department of Both Californias ... I have granted to them exclusively the said Island'. Alvarado does not appear in the grant, the petition, the deed of transfer, or the judicial possession; 'Manuel Jimeno' appears only as Secretary countersigning.

corrections.correction: Manuel Jimeno (Manuel Jimeno Casarin), 1er vocal of the Departmental Junta 'en ejercicio del Gobierno' - i.e. Governor ad interim - who signed the titulo at Monterey 26 October 1841 (PDF p22-23). Register's 'Alvarado' is wrong on the face of the grant.
corrections.evidence: The grant was NOT made by Alvarado. The titulo itself, PDF p22 (45 ND p.16), is headed: 'Manuel Jimeno Casarin 1er vocal propietario de la Excma Junta Departamental en ejercicio del Gobierno del mismo. Por cuanto el ciudadano Cayetano Juares ha pretendido... usando de las facultades que me son conferidas a nombre de la nacion Mejicana he benido en concederle el terreno mencionado declarandole la propiedad de el por las presentes letras', subscribed at PDF p23 'Manuel Jimeno / Jose L. Fernandez Srio into'. Board opinion PDF p49 (45 ND p.41): 'a grant made by Manuel Jimeno Governor ad interim'; District Court PDF p70 (45 ND p.60): 'Jimeno was, at the time Governor ad interim'. Alvarado's name appears nowhere on the instrument

corrections.correction: Manuel Jimeno (Casarin), acting governor / 'Governor ad interim', per the grant titulo (stamped p20) and DC opinion (transcript p172). NOT Alvarado.
corrections.evidence: Grant (titulo/despacho) in the expediente signed 'Man'l Jimeno... primer vocal de la Exma. Junta de este Departamento, EN EJERCICIO DEL GOB[IERN]O del mismo' (Manuel Jimeno Casarin, acting governor), Monterey Dec 15 1840 (stamped pp20-21). US District Court opinion (transcript p172): 'The claim in this case is founded upon a grant from Manuel Jimeno, Governor ad interim of California, to one Gabriel De la Torre, bearing date the 20th August 1839.' The 'Alvarado. Antonio M. Osio' text on the 1842 deed leaf (stamped p14) is only the revenue-stamp (sello) habilitation for the paper, NOT the grantor. Register 'Alvarado' is wrong; the grant was made/signed by Manuel Jimeno (acting governor). Matches Hoffman (Manuel Jimeno).

corrections.correction: William Dickey (Sp. 'Guillermo Dickey'), per the grant decree of 18 Nov 1844, PDF p14 (PAGE 9): 'declaro á D. Guillermo Dickey mejicano por naturalizacion dueño en propiedad de un parage situado en el Rio de Sacramento'. John Bidwell was the U.S. claimant, who took title through George McKinstry Jr. in 1849 and Justus McKinstry in 1851.
corrections.evidence: THE REGISTER RECORDS THE U.S.-ERA CLAIMANT, NOT THE MEXICAN GRANTEE. The grant decree (PDF p14, PAGE 9) declares 'á D. Guillermo Dickey mejicano por naturalizacion dueño en propiedad de un parage situado en el Rio de Sacramento'; the title itself (PDF p15, PAGE 10) recites 'Por cuanto D. Guillermo Dickey mejicano por naturalizacion ha pretendido para su beneficio personal y el de su familia cinco sitios de ganado mayor, entre las margenes del Rio Sacramento ... he venido en concederle provisionalmente dho. terreno'; the expediente cover is headed '1844. Espediente promovido por D. Guillermo Dickey en solicitud del terreno que se espresa' (PDF p10, PAGE 5). Bidwell's own petition says so plainly (PDF p9, PAGE 4): 'That on the 18th Nov. 1844 a grant of five leagues was made with a provisional title to William Dickey by Gov. Micheltorena ... that said grant was sold and conveyed to Geo. McKinstry Jr. by deed dated 7th May 1849 who conveyed one undivided half thereof to your Petitioner by deed dated July 4th 1849'. The District Court index lists the chain: 'Deed Dickey to McKinstry / Deed McKinstry to Bidwell / Dickey to Bidwell - derivation of title to Bidwell' (PDF p138, PAGE 123). Hoffman's 'William Dickey' agrees with the case file against the register.

corrections.correction: Charles William (Carlos Guillermo) Flugge, per grant of 21 Feb 1844, stamped PAGES 30-33; Larkin took by conveyance of 21 Jan 1847 (stamped PAGES 11, 85)
corrections.evidence: Grant, stamped PAGE 30: 'Por cuanto Don Carlos Guillermo Flugge mejicano por naturalizacion... he venido en concederle el terreno mencionado'; translation stamped PAGE 32: 'Whereas Charles William Flugge... I have come to the conclusion to grant unto the petitioner the above mentioned lands'. Larkin was only the purchaser-claimant: 'a deed of conveyance from the said Flugge dated the 21st day of January 1847' (Board opinion, stamped PAGE 85). Register records the U.S.-era claimant, not the Mexican grantee.

corrections.correction: Jose Joaquin de la Torre (grant of June 22, 1822); Cooper is claimant/purchaser only. Per decree transcript p10-11: 'le concedo a nombre de S.M. Imperial la gracia que solicita... de las Bolsas del Potrero y Moro Cojo'.
corrections.evidence: Original grantee = Jose Joaquin de la Torre, 'Cadete de la Compania de Caballeria de este Imperial Presidio de Monterey' (petition + Sola's decree, transcript p9-11, PDF p13-15). John B. R. Cooper was the PURCHASER: de la Torre sold him the rancho by escritura of Oct 2, 1829 before alcalde Jose Tiburcio Castro (transcript p12-15, PDF p16-19), and Cooper acquired Milligan's half from executor Hartnell Aug 21, 1834 (transcript p16-17, PDF p20-21). Hoffman's 'F. Tico' is also wrong.

corrections.register_value: Thomas O. Larkin and John S. Missroon
corrections.correction: Manuel Jimeno, per the grant of 4 Nov 1844 (translation PDF p30: 'Whereas Don Manuel Jimeno has petitioned ... I have just granted to him the said land'); Larkin and Missroon took by deed 30 Aug 1847 and were only the claimants
corrections.evidence: The grantee was Don Manuel Jimeno, not the claimants. Grant translation, PDF p30 (case p24): 'Whereas Don Manuel Jimeno has petitioned for his personal benefit for the tract of land which is unoccupied between the Ranch which has been granted to the children of Don Tomas O. Larkin, the River Sacramento ... I have just granted to him the said land'. Expediente decree PDF p25 (case p19): 'declaro a D. Manuel Jimeno dueño de once sitios de ganado mayor'. Larkin and Missroon are the PURCHASERS under the deed of conveyance of 30 August 1847 (PDF p21-22, case p15-16: 'comparecio D.n Manuel Jimeno y dijo: que ... vende y da en venta publica ... a D.n Tomas O. Larkin ... y a D.n Juan S. Missroon'), and thereby the U.S.-era claimants. District Court opinion PDF p139 (case p134) states it flatly: 'The original grant by Governor Micheltoreno to Manuel Jimeno bears date November 1844. The conveyance to the present claimants is dated August 30. 1847.'

corrections.correction: María Antonia Estudillo de Pedrorena, per the grant decree of 23 Sept 1845 (PDF p23 / case p16: 'declaro a Da. Maria Antonia Estudillo de Pedrorena dueña del terreno nombrado "Cajon"'). T. W. Sutherland was guardian of her four minor children and the claimant before the Board, not the grantee.
corrections.evidence: The grantee was Doña María Antonia Estudillo de Pedrorena. Grant decree PDF p23 (case p16): 'declaro a Da. Maria Antonia Estudillo de Pedrorena dueña del terreno nombrado "Cajon" inmediato a la predicha Mision de S.n Diego'; translation PDF p31 (case p24). The expediente is captioned 'Espediente promovido por Da. Maria Antonia Estudillo de Pedrorena, en solicitud del terreno nombrado el Cajon' (PDF p15, case p9). Thomas W. Sutherland is the U.S.-era CLAIMANT only, in the capacity of guardian: petition PDF p9 (case p4) is brought for 'Victoria, Isabel, Miguel and Helena Minor children of Miguel de Pedrorena and Maria Antonia Estudillo de Pedrorena ... both deceased', and the Supreme Court mandate PDF p81 (case p67) styles the appellee 'Thomas W. Sutherland, Guardian of Victoria, Isabel, Miguel, and Helena, minor children & heirs of Miguel de Pedrorena and Maria Antonia Estudillo de Pedrorena, deceased'. Witness Santiago Argüello likewise calls her 'the Original grantee' (PDF p12, case p6).

corrections.correction: Guillermo (William) Gulnac, per the grant of 13 Jan 1844 quoted in the Board opinion, PDF p110 (case p100): 'Whereas Don Guillermo Gulnac Mexican by Naturalization has asked for his own personal benefit and that of his family, and Eleven other families for the land known by the name of "Campo de los Franceses"'; and Commissioner Farwell, PDF p113 (case p103): 'The grant then was to Gulnac.' Charles M. Weber bought Gulnac's interest by deed of 3 April 1845 and was the claimant before the Board.
corrections.evidence: The grantee was Don Guillermo (William) Gulnac; Weber was the purchaser and U.S.-era claimant. Grant decree as quoted in the Board opinion, PDF p110 (case p100): 'Whereas Don Guillermo Gulnac Mexican by Naturalization has asked for his own personal benefit and that of his family, and Eleven other families for the land known by the name of "Campo de los Franceses" in extent Eleven Square leagues between the Rio de San Joaquin on the East and the Laguna called McCloud...'; PDF p111 (case p101): 'I have granted to him the said Land declaring to him the Ownership of it by these letters'. Commissioner Farwell states it flatly at PDF p113 (case p103): 'The grant then was to Gulnac.' corrections.evidence: The grant ran to LUIS ARENAS and JUAN (JOHN) ROLAND, not to Roland and Hornsby. Luis Arenas conveyed his interest to James M Jones, who died and devised all his property to the Appellant J.L. Hornsby.' Hoffman ('Luis Arenas and John Roland') agrees with the case file against the register.

corrections.correction: Pedro Narvaez per the concession decree, PDF p21 (351 SD PAGE 16): 'declaro dueno en propiedad a D.n Pedro Narvaez del parage conocido con el nombre de Paso de Robles'. Petronilo Rios acquired it from Narvaez, first by an act of assignment endorsed on the grant 5 April 1845 and then by a formal deed of sale before the 1st Alcalde of Monterey, 30 March 1846 (petition PDF p9, PAGE 4; deed PDF p23, PAGE 28, signed Manuel Diaz, alcalde, and Pedro Narvaez).
corrections.evidence: PDF p21 (PAGE 16), the decree itself: 'declaro dueno en propiedad a D.n Pedro Narvaez del parage conocido con el nombre de Paso de Robles'. The expediente is headed (PDF p18, PAGE 13) '1844 Espediente. Promovido por el Sor. Capitan D.n Pedro Narvaes en solicitud del parage conocido con el nombre de Paso de Robles. Numero 375', and the underlying petition (PDF p20, PAGE 15) is signed 'Monterrey Nov.e 26 de 1843. Pedro Narvaez', describing himself as '1er teniente de la armada nacional y capitan de este puerto'. Petronilo Rios is the U.S.-era claimant, a purchaser: the Board's own opinion (PDF p36) says 'The petitioner in this case asks a confirmation as grantee of Don Pedro Narvaez ... and also a deed from the said Narvaez to the present claimant dated the 30th day of March 1846.'

corrections.correction: Francisco Estrada per the grant, PDF p20/p24 (97 ND PAGES 16 and 20). Mariano Castro took by conveyance from Jose Maria Estrada, Francisco's father and heir: the cession endorsed on the back of the title reads 'Como heredero del finado Francisco Estrada, digo que cedo voluntariamente a favor del ciud.no Mariano Castro, los dos sitios que se espresan en este titulo. Buenavista, 17 de Marzo 1845. Jose Maria Estrada' (PDF p21, PAGE 17; English at PDF p26, PAGE 22), judicially authenticated before Regidor Ignacio Esquer at San Jose on 27 January 1846 (PDF p27 and p29, PAGES 18-19).
corrections.evidence: The grant itself, PDF p20 (97 ND PAGE 16): 'Por cuanto D. Francisco Estrada, ha pretendido para su beneficio personal y el de su familia, el terreno conocido con el nombre de Pastoria de las Borregas ... he venido en concederle el terreno mencionado, declarando le la propiedad de el por las presentes letras.' Sworn translation PDF p24 (PAGE 20): 'Whereas D.n Francisco Estrada has sought to obtain for his personal benefit & that of his family the tract of land known by the name of Pastoria de las Borregas ... I have conceded to him the said tract of land, declaring to him the ownership thereof by these present letters.' Mariano Castro is the U.S.-era claimant only. The Board's own opinion, PDF p39 (PAGE 34), states it plainly: 'on the 2d day of January A.D. 1842, one Don Francisco Estrada obtained from Governor Alvarado a grant for the place called Pastoria de los Borregas, that some time in the year 1845 the said grantee died, without wife or children ... that the father of said grantee, as heir of his son Francisco ... conveyed all his interest in & to said tract of land to the petitioner in this case.'

corrections.register_value: Hiram Grimes, Francis W. Grimes and William H. McKee
corrections.correction: Valentin (Balentin) Higuera and Rafael Feliz, per grant decree translation p31-33 and Commission opinion p41. Register value (Grimes/McKee) names the US-era claimants/assignees, not the Mexican grantees. Hoffman 1862 ('Valentin Higuera and Rafael Feliz') agrees with the case file against the register.
corrections.evidence: grant decree translation p31: 'Whereas the Citizens Balentin Higuera and Rafael Feliz have petitioned... I have just granted to them'; Commission opinion p41 'a grant made by Governor Micheltorena to Balentin Higuera and Rafael Feliz'. Register lists Grimes/McKee, who are downstream CLAIMANTS (McKee by deed 1849; Grimes via Feliz->Cecena->Grimes deeds 1848), not the original grantees.

corrections.register_value: José de la Guerra y Noriega
corrections.correction: Jose Carrillo, per concession decree May 15, 1834 (transcript p19: 'se declara a D. Jose Carrillo dueno en propiedad del terreno... las Posas') and Board decree (transcript p62); register's 'Jose de la Guerra y Noriega' is the 1846 purchaser/claimant, who belongs in patent_to, not grantee
corrections.evidence: Original grantee is JOSE CARRILLO, not Jose de la Guerra y Noriega. Concession decree (pdf p24, transcript p19): 'se declara a D. Jose Carrillo dueno en propiedad del terreno conocido con el nombre de las Posas'; titulo (pdf p26, transcript p21): 'Por cuanto D. Jose Carrillo mejicano por nacimiento...'; Diputacion approval May 22, 1834 of 'la concesion hecha al Ciudadano Jose Carrillo' (pdf p25, transcript p20); Board decree (pdf p69, transcript p62): 'being the same which was granted to Jose Carrillo, by Governor Jose Figueroa on the 28th day of July 1834'. De la Guerra y Noriega was the PURCHASER (deed from Carrillo, June 27, 1846, petition pdf p9, transcript p4) and the claimant before the Board.

corrections.correction: Lope Inigo (an emancipated neophyte of Mission Santa Clara), per the District Court's own words 'the grant to Inigo, the original grantee' (PDF p124 / stamped p119) and the Spanish decree 'declaro al Yndigena de Sta Clara dueno de un terreno que se nombra Posolmi' (PDF p75 / stamped p71). Register 'Robert Walkinshaw' is the U.S.-era claimant who bought half the rancho from Inigo by deeds of 9 June 1849 and 31 July 1850 (PDF p11 / stamped p7). Hoffman 1862 ('Lope Inigo') agrees with the case file against the register. This is a textbook instance of the dominant error class.
corrections.evidence: U.S. District Court survey-contest pleading, PDF p124 (stamped 410ND p119): 'The land confirmed to Claimants is the land laid down in the diseno or map which accompanied the petition for the grant, and is referred to in the grant to Inigo, THE ORIGINAL GRANTEE.' Spanish decree in the archive expediente, PDF p75 (stamped p71): 'declaro al Yndigena de Sta Clara dueno de un terreno que se nombra Posolmi colindante con el sausal, al Sur con el Estero, al Nte con su casa y el ojo de agua que llaman Positas de las animitas. hagasele el correspondiente [titulo].' Supplemental petition of Lope Inigo himself, PDF p13 (stamped p9): 'Micheltorena... granted to your petitioner a tract of land called Poslmi'. Robert Walkinshaw is the U.S.-era CLAIMANT/purchaser: PDF p11 (stamped p7) 'the said Inigo sold and conveyed to the Petitioner one half of the said tract of land, viz: 3042 acres... by the deeds of conveyance dated June 9th 1849 and July 31st 1850'.

corrections.correction: Fructuoso del Real (also written Fructuoso de Jesus del Real), a neophyte/native of Mission San Carlos, per the expediente and its sworn translation (PDF p25, p29, p30 = stamped p20, p25, p26) and the Commission opinion (PDF p47 = stamped p40). Register 'Joaquin Gutierrez' names the U.S.-era claimant, who bought in from the grantee's widow Yginia in 1845 and again by deed of 7 April 1852. Hoffman 1862 ('Fructuoso') agrees with the case file against the register. Dominant error class.
corrections.evidence: Expediente cover PDF p25 (stamped p20): 'Espediente promovido por Frutuoso del Real en pretencion del paraje nombrado el Potrero. No 115'; translation PDF p29 (stamped p25): 'Espediente moved by Fructuoso del Real asking for the place called "El Potrero"... Fructuoso del Real, a native of the Mission of San Carlos, before Your Excellency in due and legal form appears... praying that you will be so good as to grant him the place known by the name of "El Potrero"'; Mission report PDF p30 (stamped p26): 'The Petitioner Fructuoso del Real is a Neophyte of this Mission'. Commission opinion PDF p47 (stamped p40) calls him 'one Fructuosa an Indian' and says 'the grantee died some years since leaving a wife and three children his heirs'. Joaquin Gutierrez is the U.S.-era CLAIMANT: his own petition PDF p7 (stamped p4) states that Alvarado 'granted to one Fructuoso' and that the widow Yginia 'sold and conveyed the said tract of land to the petitioner' in 1845, re-conveying 7 April 1852.

corrections.register_value: Samuel G. Reed and Ruben S. Wade
corrections.correction: Original grantees were Mariano and Pedro Hernandez (brothers, of Pueblo de San José Guadalupe), per the concession decree of 18 Jan 1844: 'I declare Citizens Mariano and Pedro Hernandez to be the Owners of Three Square Leagues' (translation stamp p25) / 'declaro dueños de tres sitios de ganado mayor' (Spanish stamp p21), and the expediente cover 'promovido por los C.C. Mariano y Pedro Hernandez' (stamp p19). The register lists the U.S. claimants Samuel G. Reid (register: 'Reed') and Reuben S. Wade, who bought via Hiram Grimes.
corrections.evidence: The grant declares the grantees to be Mariano and Pedro Hernandez, NOT the register's American claimants. Expediente cover, Spanish (stamp p19, image 12 of batch2): 'Espediente promovido por los C.C. Mariano y Pedro Hernandez en solicitud del parage que se espresa. Numero 321.' Petition (stamp p20): 'Mariano y Pedro Hernandez hermanos y vecinos del pueblo de San José Guadalupe.' Concession decree translation (stamp p25, image 18): 'I declare Citizens Mariano and Pedro Hernandez to be the Owners of Three Square Leagues.' The register's 'Samuel G. Reed and Ruben S. Wade' (of Boston) are the CLAIMANTS/purchasers: the Hernandez brothers sold to Hiram Grimes 16 Aug 1847, and Grimes conveyed to Reid/Reed and Wade 11 June 1850 (petition, stamp p5).

corrections.correction: Jose Francisco (Joseph Francis) Snook per Board decree p61; register's Berry is the 1836 grantee of the surrounding tract (grant by Gutierrez, petition p5)
corrections.evidence: Board decree p61: the confirmed land is 'the same land granted to Jose Francisco Snook by Governor Alvarado on the 8th day of June 1839'. Berry (register's grantee) was the 1836 grantee of the surrounding tract who expressly released these 2 leagues to Snook (petition p5, p8-9); title chain confirmed: Snook -> Osio (28 Sept 1839) -> Randall (8 Jan 1852) (opinion p59)

corrections.correction: Jose Gorgonio and his son Jose Ramon, emancipated neophytes of Mission Santa Clara, per the sworn translation of Alvarado's grant of 30 June 1840 (PDF p27 / stamped p22) and the Board's opinion (PDF p32 / stamped p27). Juana Briones de Miranda bought the rancho from them for $300 by deed of 7 November 1844, executed before the alcalde of San Jose with Micheltorena's licence; she is the U.S.-era claimant, not the grantee. Hoffman 1862 ('Jose Gorgonio and Jose Ramon') agrees with the case file against the register. Dominant error class.
corrections.evidence: Grant translation, PDF p27 (stamped p22): 'Whereas Gorgonio, a neophyte of the ex-mission of Santa Clara, has, in his own name & in that of his son Jose Ramon, petitioned for the place named La Purisima Concepcion... I HAVE BY THESE PRESENTS GRANTED TO SAID GORGONIO & TO HIS SON JOSE RAMON, the ownership of the aforementioned place of La Purisima Concepcion, in extent one sitio de ganado mayor (one square league).' Board's opinion PDF p32 (stamped p27): 'founded on a grant made by Governor Juan B. Alvarado, to an emancipated Neophyte of the Mission of Santa Clara, named Gorgonio & his son Jose Ramon... The present claimant derives her title by virtue of a conveyance made to her with the sanction of the Government BY THE SAID GRANTEES Gorgonio & Jose Ramon on the 7th of November 1844.' Juana Briones is the purchaser/claimant, not the grantee: her own 1852 petition PDF p9 (stamped p4) says Alvarado 'granted to Jose Gregorio & his son Jose Ramon, emancipated Neophytes of the Mission of Santa Clara... the tract of land known by the name of La Purisima Concepcion', and that they 'sold & conveyed in due form to the petitioner' on 7 Nov 1844.

corrections.correction: Jose de Jesus Berreyesa and Sisto Berreyesa, brothers, per Micheltorena's grant of 3 November 1843 as recited in the Board's opinion (PDF p69 / stamped p58) and its decree (PDF p72 / stamped p61). Maria Anastasia Higuera de Berreyesa and Maria Nicolasa Higuera de Berreyesa are the WIVES of the two grantees and took by deed from their husbands; they are the named U.S.-era claimants (and, per the register, the patentees). Hoffman 1862 ('Jose de Jesus y Sisto Berreyesa') agrees with the case file against the register. A variant of the dominant error class: the register carries the claimant/patentee rather than the Mexican grantee.
corrections.evidence: Board's opinion PDF p69 (stamped p58): the grant was 'made by Governor Manuel Micheltorena TO THE BROTHERS JOSE DE JESUS AND SISTO BERRYESA'. PDF p72 (stamped p61) is explicit about the register's confusion: 'Among the documentary evidence introduced into this case are two deeds of the premises claimed, one from Jose de Jesus Berryesa to Anastasia Higuera, HIS WIFE, and the other from Sisto Berryesa to Nicolasa Higuera HIS WIFE. The Petition in the case asks a confirmation in the name of these two grantees, THE WIVES OF THE PERSONS TO WHOM THE ORIGINAL GRANT WAS MADE BY THE GOVERNOR. If the husbands were not themselves joined as petitioners in this case a question not free from difficulty would arise as to the effect of the conveyances from husband to wife.' Claimants' petition PDF p11 (stamped p5) likewise: 'on the 11th day of February 1842 the said Jose Jesus Berryesa and Sisto Berryesa... made their Petition in writing signed by them addressed to the Military Commandant of Sonoma praying for license to occupy provisionally eight sitios de ganado mayor... the said land being known as Las Putas.'

corrections.correction: Jose Z. Fernandez and Jose Noriega, per decree of concession 12 Mar 1841 / formal title 16 Mar 1841 (transcript pp.22-25): 'declaro a Dn Jose Z. Fernandez y a Dn Jose Noriega duenos del parage nombrado Quito'. Manuel Alviso is claimant/patentee only (suggest keeping him in patent_to, not grantee)
corrections.evidence: the grant runs to Jose Z. Fernandez and Jose Noriega, NOT Manuel Alviso: decree of concession transcript p.22 (image 28) 'declaro a Dn Jose Z. Fernandez y a Dn Jose Noriega duenos del parage nombrado Quito'; Board opinion transcript p.60 (image 70): 'a grant... made to Jose Z. Fernandez and Jose Noriega bearing date March 16th 1841 and signed by Governor Juan B. Alvarado'. Manuel Alviso was the CLAIMANT, deriving title via Noriega's 1844 sale to Ygnacio Alviso and Ygnacio's will (petition, transcript pp.4-5, images 8-9)

corrections.correction: Ygnacio (Ignacio) Alviso, per the Board's decree ('were originally granted said Ygnacio Alvisa', PDF p52 / stamped p44) and its opinion (PDF p51 / stamped p43). Francisco Berreyesa and his siblings are the grantee's great-grandchildren-in-line: Alviso (d. 10 Aug 1848) devised this north-west half to his daughter Dolores Alviso, who married Guadalupe Berreyesa; both died in the autumn of 1857 and their children Francisco, Susana, Paulina, Pancho and Guadalupe Berreyesa filed as heirs. Hoffman 1862 ('Ygnacio Alvisu') agrees with the case file against the register. Dominant error class.
corrections.evidence: Board's DECREE, PDF p52 (stamped p44): the premises 'were ORIGINALLY GRANTED SAID YGNACIO ALVISA'. Opinion PDF p51 (stamped p43): 'The Claimants are the children of Guadalupe Berryesa and Dolores Alviso his wife, both of whom died in the Autumn of 1857. The petitioners claim the property by inheritance from the Mother as her heirs at Law. HER TITLE WAS DERIVED UNDER THE WILL OF HER FATHER YGNACIO ALVISO... By the provisions of the Will the Land claimed in this Case was bequeathed to Dolores, the daughter of the testator and Mother of the claimants.' Claimants' own petition PDF p9 (stamped p4) says Alvarado 'granted to Ygnacio Alviso THE GRANDFATHER OF YOUR PETITIONERS ON THEIR MOTHER'S SIDE'. Francisco Berreyesa is thus a grandson of the grantee and one of the U.S.-era claimants, not the grantee.

corrections.correction: Ygnacio (Ignacio) Alviso per the concession of 10 Feb 1838 and Departmental Assembly approval 30 May 1840 (transcript pp.19-23): 'he venido en concederle la propiedad' / 'en la persona del ciudadano Ygnacio Alviso'. Rafael Alviso was a grandson and lead claimant-heir (child of Domingo Alviso, deceased son of grantee Ygnacio), not the original grantee
corrections.evidence: The GRANT runs to Ygnacio (Ignacio) Alviso, NOT Rafael. Spanish concession (image 27, transcript p.19): 'Ygnacio Alviso Mejicano por nacimiento ha pretendido... he venido en concederle la propiedad'; Departmental Assembly approval 30 May 1840 (image 28): 'en la persona del ciudadano Ygnacio Alviso'; English Exhibit B (image 29): 'Issuance deed given at the Petition of Ignacio Alviso'; Board opinion (image 44): 'granted... to Ygnacio Alviso'. Rafael Alviso is a claimant-heir (grandson via Domingo), not the grantee

corrections.correction: Ygnacio (Ignacio) Alviso, per the Board's opinion and decree (PDF p65, p67 = stamped p58, p60). Ellen E. White is the U.S.-era claimant: her late husband Charles White bought this eastern strip from Alviso's executor Agustin Alviso in late August 1848 for $2,000 under the power in the will, and conveyed it to her 4 November 1851. Hoffman 1862 ('Ygnacio Alvisu') agrees with the case file against the register. Dominant error class.
corrections.evidence: Board's opinion PDF p65 (stamped p58): the tract 'was GRANTED TO YGNACIO ALVISO by Governor Juan B. Alvarado February 10, 1838'; decree PDF p67 (stamped p60): the lands confirmed 'are a part of the place called Rincon de los Esteros in Santa Clara County FORMERLY OCCUPIED BY YGNACIO ALVISO'. Ellen E. White's own petition, PDF p9 (stamped p4), states the whole derivative chain: Alviso died 8 Aug 1848 leaving a will directing that the portion between the Coyote and Penitencia creeks 'be sold for the payment of his debts'; 'in pursuance thereof the said portion of said Rancho was duly sold in legal form and purchased by CHARLES WHITE of said County on the 28th day of August A.D. 1848. That on the 4th of November A.D. 1851 said Charles White sold and conveyed said land to your Petitioner by deed of that date.' Ellen E. White is therefore the second purchaser downstream of the grantee's executor.

corrections.correction: Original grantee = Tomas M. Hardy (also Tomas Hardy), per grant decree/petition PDF p15: 'granted to Tomas M. Hardy called also Tomas Hardy the tract of land called Rio de Jesus Maria'. Register's 'James M. Harbin' is the American claimant/purchaser, not the grantee.
corrections.evidence: Petition PDF p15 names ORIGINAL grantee as 'Tomas M. Hardy called also Tomas Hardy'. James M. Harbin is a claimant/purchaser: PDF p16-17 (transcript p10-11) show Hardy died intestate 1848, tract sold by probate to petitioners Harbin, Estell, Tyler, Parrish; Tyler then conveyed to Harbin. Hoffman 'Tomas Hardy' agrees against the register.

corrections.correction: Prado Mesa (styled 'el Alferez Prado Meza' / 'the Sub Lieutenant Prado Mesa') per the concession of 24 March 1839 (Exhibits A and B, transcript pp.22-25): 'he venido en concederle el terreno mencionado' / 'I have determined to grant him the said land'. Encarnacion Mesa was a child and lead claimant-heir, one of the seven children of the deceased grantee Prado Mesa, not the original grantee
corrections.evidence: The GRANT runs to Alferez / Sub-Lieutenant Prado Mesa, NOT Encarnacion. Spanish grant Exhibit A (image 29, transcript p.22): 'Por cuanto el Alferez Prado Meza ha pretendido para su beneficio personal y el de su familia el terreno... he venido en concederle el terreno mencionado'; English Exhibit B (image 31): 'Whereas the Sub Lieutenant Prado Mesa has petitioned... I have determined to grant him the said land'; Departmental Assembly approval (images 33-34, transcript pp.26-27): 'the grant which the government made to Dn Prado Mesa'; Board decree (image 57, transcript p.48): 'granted by Governor Alvarado to Prado Mesa'. Petition (transcript p.4, image 9) states the petitioners (Encarnacion, Antonio, Majin, Francisca, Ramon, Cristiano and Nicandro Mesa) are the surviving heirs of the original grantee, their father Prado (Pedro) Mesa

corrections.correction: Miguel de Pedrorena, per the grant decree PDF p19 (transcript p13): 'Por cuanto D.n Miguel de Pedrorena ha pretendido para su beneficio personal y el de su familia ... he venido en acordar de este dia en concederle el terreno mencionado y Potrero'. 'T. W. Sutherland, guardian' is the U.S. land-commission claimant, guardian of Pedrorena's minor children Victoria, Isabel, Miguel and Helena, and never a grantee.
corrections.evidence: The grant decree names MIGUEL DE PEDRORENA, not Sutherland. PDF p19 (transcript p13): 'Por cuanto D.n Miguel de Pedrorena ha pretendido para su beneficio personal y el de su familia el terreno nombrado ... y Potrero del mismo nombre ... he venido en acordar de este dia en concederle el terreno mencionado y Potrero, declarandole la propiedad de el por las presentes letras.' Translation PDF p22 (transcript p17): 'Whereas Don Miguel de Pedrorena has pretended to for his personal benefit & that of his family the land called San Jacinto Nuevo, including the Potrero of the same name.' Thomas W. Sutherland was the U.S.-era claimant only, in his capacity as GUARDIAN of Pedrorena's four orphaned minor children: petition PDF p11 (transcript p4), 'Thomas W. Sutherland ... Guardian of Victoria, Isabel, Miguel, & Helena minor children of Miguel de Pedrorena & Maria Antonia Estudillo de Pedrorena, both late of the County of San Diego ... deceased'. Pedrorena died in the spring of 1850 (J. J. Warner deposition PDF p14, transcript p7). Hoffman's 'Miguel Pedrorena' agrees against the register.

corrections.correction: Cruz Cervantes, per grant translation stamped p.138: 'Whereas Citizen Cruz Cervantes... to grant to him the aforementioned parcel of land'
corrections.evidence: Grant translation stamped p.138: 'Whereas Citizen Cruz Cervantes, a Mexican by birth, has applied for his own benefit & that of his family for the parcel of land known by the name of San Joaquin... I have thought proper by a decree of this day's date and in the name of the Mexican Nation, to grant to him the aforementioned parcel of land'. The grantee is Cruz Cervantes, who is also the claimant (red label p1). 'G. C. Yount' appears nowhere in this case file.

corrections.correction: Maximo Alanis, not Antonio del Valle. Grant decree PDF p18 (transcript p14): 'Por cuanto el Ciudadano Maximo Alaniz, ha pretendido para su beneficio personal i el de su familia el parage conocido con el nombre de San Jose Buenos Ayres'.
corrections.evidence: The grantee is MAXIMO ALANIS. Grant decree PDF p18 (transcript p14): 'Por cuanto el Ciudadano Maximo Alaniz, ha pretendido para su beneficio personal i el de su familia el parage conocido con el nombre de San Jose Buenos Ayres ... he venido en concederle el terreno mencionado declarandole la propiedad de el por las presentes letras'. Judicial possession was given to him 6 April 1846: PDF p21 (transcript p17) 'anuente a la solicitud verval que hizo Don Macsimo Alanis para que se le de posecion juridica de un terreno conocido con el nombre de San Jose Buenos Ayres'. His son Marcos Alanis deposed PDF p13-14 (transcript p9-10): 'To whom was that rancho first originally granted...? To My Father ... My Father, Maximo Alanis ... continued in the occupation of said Rancho until his death which I believe took place in the Year 1851.' Wilson and Sanford are purchasers from the heirs (petition PDF p7-8). 'Antonio del Valle' appears nowhere in this file; he is the grantee of a different rancho. Hoffman agrees against the register.

corrections.correction: Francisco Soto, not Barbara Soto. Board decree caption PDF p129 (transcript p112): 'Barbara Soto et al in trust for the Heirs of Francisco Soto dec.d'. Barbara is the widow and lead U.S.-era claimant; her co-claimants are the seven Soto children.
corrections.evidence: The grantee was FRANCISCO SOTO; Barbara Soto is his widow and the U.S.-era claimant, suing for his heirs. Board decree caption PDF p129 (transcript p112): 'Barbara Soto et al in trust for the Heirs of Francisco Soto dec.d vs The United States.' Petition PDF p11 (transcript p5): 'said land was granted to Francisco Soto ... Said Francisco Soto died prior to the filing of this petition and about seven years ago, leaving the said D.a Barbara his widow, and the said other claimants his Children and only heirs'. Guillermo Castro, PDF p13 (transcript p6): 'I was acquainted with Francesco Soto who died about seven years ago. He left a widow named Barbara Castro and seven children'. W. H. Davis, PDF p14 (transcript p7): 'Are you acquainted with the Rancho San Lorenzo claimed in this case and did you know the grantee Francesco Soto'. Hoffman's 'Francisco Soto' agrees against the register.

corrections.correction: Rafael Estrada, per the grant decree PDF p22 (transcript p16): 'Por cuanto D. Rafael Estrada ha pretendido para su beneficio personal el terreno conocido con el nombre de San Lucas ... he venido en concederle el terreno mencionado'. James McKinlay is the U.S.-era claimant, who bought from Estrada and his wife Concepcion by deed of 14 December 1850 (PDF p9, p13).
corrections.evidence: The grantee was RAFAEL ESTRADA, not McKinlay. Grant decree PDF p22 (transcript p16): 'Por cuanto D. Rafael Estrada ha pretendido para su beneficio personal el terreno conocido con el nombre de San Lucas, colindante con el rancho de D. Mariano Soberanes, con el de San Benito, con la Sierra de San Antonio y las Lomas bajas que dividen el terreno de San Lorenzo ... he venido en concederle el terreno mencionado declarandole la propiedad de el por las presentes letras'; expediente cover PDF p14 (transcript p8) 'Espediente promovido por el Ciudadano Rafael Estrada en pretencion del terreno llamado San Lucas'. McKinlay's own petition PDF p9 (transcript p4) says he 'claims the same in fee by virtue of a grant made unto Raphael Estrada ... by John B. Alvarado, Constitutional Governor of the Californias, bearing date the ninth of May A.D. 1842 ... which said grantee Raphael Estrada did transfer in due form by a deed bearing date the fourteenth of December 1850 unto your petitioner all his right, title & interest'. W. S. Johnson, Recorder of Monterey County, authenticated that deed, PDF p13 (transcript p7): 'a transfer of certain property known as the Rancho de San Lucas by Rafael Estrada & his wife to James McKinlay dated December 14th A.D. 1850'. Hoffman's 'Rafael Estrada' agrees against the register.

corrections.correction: Jose Maria Mejia and Juan Perez Pacheco per grant decree transcript p7 (Mejia conveyed his half to Pacheco 7 Nov 1843 per petition transcript p5)
corrections.evidence: Grant decree (PDF p11, transcript p7): 'el Capitan Dn Jose Maria Mejia... y Dn Juan Perez Pacheco... he venido en concederla el terreno mencionado'. DC opinion (transcript p67): 'he declares Jose M. Mejia & Juan Perez Pacheco owners of the tract known as San Luis Gonzaga'. Francisco Rivera was the forfeited prior (1841) grantee, not the grantee of the confirmed grant. Hoffman also lists Rivera; the case file overrules both.

corrections.correction: Raimundo (Reimundo) Olivas and Felipe Lorenzana, per the grant decree PDF p13/p15: 'los ciudadanos Reimundo Olivas y Felipe Lorenzana'
corrections.evidence: Grant decree PDF p13 (transcript p8): 'Por cuanto los ciudadanos Reimundo Olivas y Felipe Lorenzana han pretendido para sus beneficios personales y el de sus familias, el terreno que media al Sur con el Rio de Santa Clara...he venido en concederles el terreno mencionado'; translation PDF p15 (transcript p10): 'Whereas the citizens Raimundo Olivas & Felipe Lorenzana have asked for their benefit...'. Register 'P. Apis' appears nowhere in the file.

corrections.correction: Marcos (Marcus) West, per the 1840 concession decree transcript p47 and Micheltorena's 1844 revalidation transcript p51
corrections.evidence: Every grant instrument names Marcos (Marcus) West: expediente cover transcript p44 (PDF p48) 'Expediente promovido por el C[iudadan]o Marcos West en solicitud del terreno que expresa'; concession decree transcript p47 (PDF p51) 'I declare Marcos West owner in fee of the place shown marked out on the map...the extent of the land being one and a half square leagues'; Micheltorena 1844 (transcript p51, PDF p55) 'Por cuanto D. Marcos West mejicano por naturaleza y casado con mejicana...'. corrections.correction: REJECTED, not Confirmed. The District Court decree of 6 March 1862 (Fletcher M. Haight, US District Judge, Southern District; transcript p226) REVERSED the Board of Land Commissioners' confirmation of 18 Dec 1855 and held the claim invalid. The grant was one of Gov. It is Ordered, Adjudged and Decreed that the decision of said Board of Land Commissioners be reversed, and that the said Claim of the Appellee is held as invalid And is hereby Rejected', Fletcher M. Haight US Dist Judge; DC Opinion transcript p228-229 (PDF stamped 228-229): 'The decision of the Board of Commissioners is reversed and the claim is rejected.' corrections.correction: 1843 (25 October) for the rancho itself. The register's 1841 is the year of a much smaller anterior title: expediente No. 1, cover PDF p23 (transcript p17), 'Jurisdiccion del Pueblo de San Jose de Alvarado. Año de 1841. Espediente promovido por el Ciudadano Guillermo Castro en solicitud de SEIS CIENTAS VARAS de terreno en el paraje de San Lorenzo'. The 1843 title expressly distinguishes the two, PDF p16 (transcript p10, condition 3): 'El terreno de que se hace donacion es de SEIS SITIOS DE GANADO MAYOR a mas de las seis cientas varas de terreno que tiene concedido por titulo anterior' (translation PDF p21/transcript p15: 'six sitios of ganado mayor, beside the six hundred varas which he holds conceded by anterior title'). The 600 varas square is a house-lot-scale parcel; the six sitios are the rancho.
corrections.evidence: The rancho grant is dated 25 October 1843, not 1841. Micheltorena's concession decree, Spanish, PDF p17 (transcript p11): 'Monterey 25 de Octubre de 1843. Vista la peticion con que da principio este espediente, los informes que preceden ... declaro a D. Guillermo Castro, dueño en propiedad del parage nombrado San Lorenzo, colindante con el Rancho de S.r Amador, con el de San Ramon, con el del S.r Moraga, con el de los Peraltas, con el del S.r Estudillo, con el del S.r Vallejo, y con el de D. Fran.co Soto'; the titulo itself closes PDF p16 (transcript p10) 'Dado en Monterrey a 25 de Ob.e de 1843'. Sworn translation PDF p20-22 (transcript p14-16): 'Monterey 25th Oct. 1843 ... I declare D.n Guillermo Castro, owner in property of the place named San Lorenzo' / 'Given in Monterey this 25th Oct 1843'. The District Judge's own bench notes, PDF p354 (transcript p340), state flatly: 'Estudillo did not obtain his grant until 1842 - & Castro not until 1843.' The register's 1841 belongs to a far smaller anterior title (see corrections).

corrections.correction: 1843 per grant decree transcript p7: 'Dado en Monterrey a cuatro de Noviembre de mil ochocientos cuarenta y tres'
corrections.evidence: Grant decree in expediente (PDF p11, transcript p7): 'Dado en Monterrey a cuatro de Noviembre de mil ochocientos cuarenta y tres' (4 Nov 1843). DC opinion (PDF p76, transcript p66): 'The claim in this case is founded on a grant made by Governor Micheltorena on the 4th November 1843.' Register's 1841 is the year of the earlier Francisco Rivera grant, which was denounced and forfeited (petition, transcript p4; DC opinion transcript p67).

corrections.correction: 1838 per the grant expediente (Alvarado deposition, transcript p14/pdf p20: 'the traced copy of the Expediente in this case for the year 1838'; petition, transcript p5/pdf p11: 'July 17 A.D. 1838'). Register's 1834 is wrong.
corrections.evidence: The grant is of 1838, not 1834. Petition (pdf p11, transcript p5): claim rests on 'a grant under the Mexican Government by Governor J. B. Alvarado... of date July 17 A.D. 1838'. Juan B. Alvarado's own deposition (pdf p20, transcript p14): 'Look at the traced copy of the Expediente in this case for the year 1838 and say what you recollect concerning the grant therein appearing to have been given Francisco Villa. Answer - I recollect there was such a grant and the signatures... appear to be mine.' Register '1834' is wrong; Hoffman 1838 agrees with the file.

corrections.correction: 1834 -- titulo 'Dado en Monterrey a primero de Agosto de mil ocho cientos treinta y cuatro' (transcript p31), on a concession decree of 22 January 1834 approved by the Diputacion 31 July 1834
corrections.evidence: The title is dated 1834, not 1835. Titulo, transcript p31 (PDF p37): 'Dado en Monterrey a primero de Agosto de mil ocho cientos treinta y cuatro' (1 August 1834). Its recitals, transcript p29 (PDF p35): 'de conformidad con el acuerdo de la Exma Diputacion Territorial del dia 31 de Julio ppdo aprobando la concesion del citado terreno de San Ramon hecha en decreto de 22 de Enero del presente año al referido Ciudno Jose Maria Amador'. Expediente proceedings run 1833-34: cover 'Año de 1833' (transcript p19, PDF p25); Figueroa's referral 'Monterrey Julio 28 de 1834...pase a la Excelentisima Diputacion Territorial para su aprobacion. Figueroa' and Diputacion action 'Monterrey Julio 29 de 1834' (transcript p27, PDF p33). The petition agrees: transcript p5 (PDF p9) 'was granted to Jose Maria Amador on the 1st day of August 1834 by Don Jose Figueroa Political Chief of the Territory of Upper California'. Hoffman's 1834 is right and the register's 1835 is wrong. The file's only 1835 item is a SEPARATE later application by Amador for an ADJACENT tract, with Figueroa's decree 'Monterrey Julio 24 de 1835' (transcript p32, PDF p38).

corrections.correction: 1846 per the grant itself (stamped p13, PDF p18): 'a treinta de Enero de mil ochocientos cuarenta y seis'; the two earlier petitions are Apr 8 1845 and Jan 30 1846, and Pico's Apr 28 1845 marginal decree only allowed provisional occupation pending title - the title issued Jan 30 1846. Hoffman 1862 (1846) agrees with the case file against the register
corrections.evidence: Spanish grant p18 (stamped p13): 'Dado en la Ciudad de los Angeles... a treinta de Enero de mil ochocientos cuarenta y seis' (Jan 30, 1846); Felch opinion p33 (stamped p27): grant 'bears date January 30th 1846'; District Court decree (stamped p78A): 'granted on the 30th day of January A.D. 1846'. Register says 1845 - wrong

corrections.correction: 1843 - grant title 'Dada en Monterey a cuatro de Octubre de mil ocho cientos cuarenta y tres' (transcript p8; translation p15-16). NOT 1841.
corrections.evidence: Grant title, transcript p8 (Spanish original) closes: 'Dada en Monterey a cuatro de Octubre de mil ocho cientos cuarenta y tres. Manl. Micheltna. Manl. Jimeno Srio.' Sworn translation, transcript pp.15-16 ('B. Translation of Grant'): 'Given at Monterey on the fourth of October one thousand eight hundred & forty three (Signed) Manuel Micheltorena (Signed) Manuel Jimeno Secretary'. Petition, transcript p4: 'That on the 4th day of October A.D. 1843 Manuel Micheltorena Governor of California ... granted to Jose Antonio Carrillo & Carlos Carrillo the tract of land called the Island of Santa Rosa'. Nothing dated 1841 appears anywhere in the pages read.

corrections.evidence: Concession decree (Spanish, stamped p16): 'Mision de San Carlos. 17 abril de 1820. En atencion a los meritos del suplicante le concedo en nombre de Ntro. Augusto Monarca el Sor. Dn. Fernando 7o ... el parage nombrado la Vega del Pajaro ... Sola'; translation (stamped p22): 'Mission of San Carlos 17th April 1820 ... I concede in the name of our August Monarch ... corrections.correction: 1841 - 'the grant was dated 22d April, 1841' (PDF p385, 342 ND p.369); register's 1834 is wrong for this title.
corrections.evidence: The grant is of 1841, not 1834. Printed brief of the settlers, PDF p385 (342 ND p.369): 'As we have seen, the grant was dated 22d April, 1841, and the measurement made and possession given in the same year. It appears from the espediente just mentioned, that in September, 1843, two years afterwards, Graham petitioned Governor Micheltorena, for a grant of the vacant land adjoining Zayante on the west'. Petition, PDF p9 (342 ND p.5): 'That on the 22d day of April 1841, Joseph L. Majors a Naturalized Citizen of Mexico solicited and obtained from the then Governor J. B. Alvarado a grant of a certain tract of land called and known by the name of Zayanta'. John Parrott's deposition, PDF p11 (342 ND p.7): 'the grant of land was made by Governor Alvarado on the 22d April 1841 in the name of Juan Jose Chrisostomo Major'. James W. Weeks's deposition, PDF p13 (342 ND p.9): 'a grant by said Alvarado to Don Juan Jose Chrisostomo Major dated April 22d 1841'
